description: We are Team IAVATORS, a group of IAV students combining our expertise in earth and agricultural sciences with STEM to build high-impact tech solutions for our society.
summary:
What if every farmer had the knowledge to make better decisions for their land?
That's the idea behind SOILSIM

SOILSIM brings together three things: planning, learning, and community.

It uses NASA Earth observation data and agronomic knowledge to help small-scale farmers choose better crop rotations and make informed decisions about their land. It also provides interactive learning tools and a farmer community where users can discover agricultural knowledge, share experiences, and learn from one another.
details:
Our Solution :

SOILSIM is a farming platform that helps small-scale farmers decide what to plant, understand their soil and plan their crops over three years.

Farmers start by entering information about their fields and selecting their priorities, such as improving soil fertility, saving water or increasing crop diversity.

SOILSIM uses historical temperature and rainfall data from NASA POWER to provide climate information for the selected region. It combines this with soil information, crop characteristics and agronomic knowledge to help farmers explore and compare different crop rotations.Farmers input localized field parameters (name, area, soil type, and pH) to anchor the simulation and recommendations in their actual micro-climate reality.

Agronomy Book:

SOILSIM is not just a crop planner. It also includes an Agronomy Book where farmers can learn about crops and soil, based on nasa data, a Farmer Community where they can share experiences and ask questions, and a Goodwill Garden that encourages members to help one another.

Our aim is to make agricultural knowledge and NASA data easier to understand and more useful in everyday farming.

Farmer Community: SOILSIM includes a social-media-inspired space designed specifically for farmers, where they can share updates, exchange experiences, ask questions, and learn from other members of the farming community.

Impact:

SOILSIM aims to make agricultural knowledge and NASA data more accessible to small-scale farmers, supporting better-informed decisions, healthier soils, and more sustainable farming practices. It also encourages knowledge-sharing and collaboration, helping farmers learn from each other rather than relying on isolated information.

Creativity & Innovation:

What makes SOILSIM different is how it transforms complex scientific data into an accessible, interactive experience. Instead of presenting farmers with technical datasets and charts, it combines a visual crop rotation simulator, gamified agricultural learning, social interaction, and a shared virtual garden to make sustainability something farmers can explore, understand, and experience.
